desc:
The spread of a block is its largest value minus its smallest value. Given nums, a window length k and a limit d, count the contiguous blocks of exactly k elements whose spread is at most d.

nums = [4, 6, 5, 9, 8, 8, 1], k = 3, d = 2
windows: [4,6,5] spread 2   [6,5,9] 4   [5,9,8] 4   [9,8,8] 1   [8,8,1] 7
result = 2
hints: Taking max and min of each window directly costs O(n * k).
You need the maximum and the minimum of a sliding window. A monotonic deque gives either in amortized O(1).

Keep one deque of indices with decreasing values (front = max) and one with increasing values (front = min). Drop front indices that fall out of the window; compare nums[maxFront] - nums[minFront] with d.
editorial: Maintain two deques of indices. In the max-deque the values are strictly decreasing from front to back, so the front is the window maximum; before pushing index i pop all back entries with value less than or equal to nums[i]. The min-deque is the mirror image. Pop from the front whenever its index is at most i - k.
Once i ≥ k - 1, the window is complete: check whether nums[maxdq[0]] - nums[mindq[0]] ≤ d and count it. Every index enters and leaves each deque at most once, so the time is O(n), with O(k) space.
